title: When stock goes up and down
text: Stock goes down when items leave and goes up when items arrive. Every stock change is recorded.
steps: Stock goes down after a paid sale, when you send a transfer, or when you write off damaged or expired items.
Stock goes up when you receive a delivery or transfer, or process a customer return.
A saved but unpaid order does not reduce stock.
Cancelling a paid receipt puts the items back in stock.
To see a product's stock history, go to Inventory > Stock on Hand and double-click the product.

title: Cancel, refund, or return: which one to use
text: Cancel a whole receipt. Refund items when the customer wants money back. Use Return or Exchange when the customer swaps items.
steps: Choose Cancel when the whole sale was a mistake. It cancels the entire receipt.
Choose Refund when the customer returns some items and wants money back.
Choose Return or Exchange when the customer swaps items.
All three return the items to stock and reduce your sales total.
Go to Point of Sale > More Options > View Sales History to use any of them.

title: What counts as your sales total
text: Gross sales is the total value of everything sold. Net sales is the amount left after deductions and extra charges are included.
steps: Start with gross sales, the full value of everything sold.
Subtract discounts, returns, refunds, and cancelled receipts.
If prices include tax, subtract the tax amount too.
Add extra charges you collected, such as a service charge. The result is net sales.

title: What each branch keeps separate
text: Stock, prices, settings, and receipts are separate for each branch. Product categories and staff accounts are shared across the store.
steps: Each branch has its own stock, prices, settings, and receipts.
Product categories are shared, so a change appears in every branch.
Staff accounts are shared. Choose which branches each staff member can access.
Reports show the selected branch. Select All Branch to see combined results.

title: When a customer owes you money
text: A customer can take the goods now and pay later. The sale is completed, and stock is reduced immediately. The unpaid balance stays on the customer's account until payment is made.
steps: On the register, click Customer and select the customer.
Click Record Payment > Unpaid. The sale is completed and stock is reduced.
To collect payment later, go to More Options > Unpaid Orders and click Pay.
The customer can pay part of the balance. The rest remains unpaid.

title: Collect an unpaid customer balance
text: You can collect all or part of a customer's unpaid balance later. Any amount left remains on the customer's account.
steps: Go to More Options > Unpaid Orders.
Find and select the customer or unpaid order.
Click Pay and enter the amount received.
Complete the payment. Any remaining balance stays as unpaid.

title: What happens when a paid receipt is cancelled
text: Cancelling a paid receipt reverses the sale. The items return to stock, and the cancelled sale is removed from your sales total.
steps: Go to Point of Sale > More Options > View Sales History.
Find and open the paid receipt.
Choose Cancel and confirm the cancellation.
Check that the items are back in stock and the sale is marked as cancelled.
keywords: what happens when sale is cancelled

title: How branch transfers change stock
text: A transfer moves items between branches. Stock decreases at the sending branch when the transfer is sent and increases at the receiving branch when it arrives.
steps: Create a transfer from the sending branch.
Send the transfer. The items leave the sending branch's stock.
Receive the transfer. The items are added to the receiving branch's stock.
Check both branches to confirm the new stock quantities.

title: When to adjust stock
text: Use a stock adjustment when the recorded quantity is wrong or items were used in the store. Enter the correct quantity and a reason so the change is recorded.
steps: Go to Inventory > Stock Adjustment.
Click New Stock Adjustment and select the product.
Enter the correct quantity and the reason.
Click Save. The stock changes immediately.

title: When to record a stock loss
text: Use Loss & Damage when items are broken, expired, stolen, or missing. The items are removed from stock and the reason is recorded.
steps: Click Sidebar > Inventory > Loss & Damage.
Click New Loss & Damage.
Select the product and enter the lost quantity.
Choose a reason, add a note (optional), and click Save.

title: Which inventory record to use
text: Choose the record that matches what happened: Stock Adjustment for a wrong number, Loss & Damage for unusable items, or Inventory Count for a physical count.
steps: Use Stock Adjustment when the recorded quantity is wrong or items were used in the store.
Use Loss & Damage when items are broken, expired, stolen, or missing.
Use Inventory Count when you count the actual items on the shelves.
Open the matching option from the Inventory menu.
